instruction: Save the video's audio as a lossless FLAC file named 'Baby Justin Bieber.flac' on the desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting audio from video and converting to lossless FLAC format using VLC. Evaluator validates: (1) File created on Desktop (30%), (2) Filename is 'Baby Justin Bieber.flac' (25%), (3) MIME type is audio/flac or audio/x-flac (30%), (4) File size exceeds 200KB (15%). Higher minimum size reflects FLAC's lossless nature. MIME check ensures genuine FLAC encoding.
metadata.verification: Verified by checking: file existence at /home/user/Desktop/Baby Justin Bieber.flac, exact filename match, MIME type verification (audio/flac or audio/x-flac) to confirm lossless format, and minimum 200KB size (higher than lossy formats) to ensure successful conversion.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: File exists (30%) + Correct filename (25%) + FLAC format verified (30%) + Valid size (15%) = 100%

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: All 4 instruction requirements verified (file existence on Desktop, correct filename, FLAC lossless format, audio extracted from video)
Getter logic correct: Uses 'file --mime-type' command to verify genuine FLAC encoding (not just file extension), reads correct file path, handles non-existence edge case
Metric logic correct: Multi-step scoring with proper partial credit (30% existence + 25% filename + 30% MIME type + 15% size), MIME type check ensures lossless format verification
Data flow correct: Getter extracts file properties and MIME type, metric validates exact filename match, FLAC format via MIME type, and reasonable 200KB minimum size for lossless audio
Expected values semantically correct: Filename matches instruction exactly, 200KB minimum appropriate for FLAC lossless format (larger than lossy formats)
Parameter handling correct: Metric uses 'expected.get("filename")' and 'expected.get("min_size")' - proper direct access to rules dict when expected.type='rule'
Practical feasibility: File accessible after VLC conversion, MIME type detection reliable, no postconfig needed for persistent file
